extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of aesthetics and Aristotelian philosophy
extracted.subtask_description: Exposition of Aristotle's theory of art and imitation as applied to the fine arts (poetry, music, painting), focusing on what arts imitate, how they imitate, and the ethical/aesthetic consequences. Useful for evaluating or producing works guided by Aristotelian criteria of imitation, semblance, and medium-specific effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Art supplements and follows nature
rubrics_metrics.description: “Art in its widest acceptation has, like nature, certain ends in view... useful art, which learns from nature the precise end at which to aim... The function, then, of the useful arts is in all cases ‘to supply the deficiencies of nature’.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful art both supplements what nature fails to complete and imitates nature's methods. Art selects ends (goals) by studying nature and aims to make good nature's defects (e.g., medicine restoring health). Failures are often due to limitations in materials rather than faulty intention. The artist/practitioner should study natural principles to discover proper ends and employ methods suggested by nature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mastery requires discerning nature's true ends and using nature's method
rubrics_metrics.description: “He who would be a master in any art must first discern the true end by a study of nature's principles, and then employ the method which she suggests for the attainment of that end.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To produce effective art/practice, identify the end/goal modeled by nature, then adapt the natural method appropriate to that end. This is a procedural requirement for competent workmanship in 'useful' arts and an evaluative standard for judging mastery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fine art's proper objects: ἤθη, πάθη, πράξεις (characters, emotions, actions)
rubrics_metrics.description: “The actual objects of aesthetic imitation are threefold—ἤθη, πάθη, πράξεις. By ἤθη are meant the characteristic moral qualities... πάθη denotes the more transient emotions... πράξεις are actions in their proper and inward sense.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Art should aim to imitate the inward mental life: stable dispositions (character), transient emotions, and inwardly grounded actions. An act is aesthetic only insofar as it springs from inward will or elicits thought/feeling, not merely as an external event. Landscape or animal depiction is secondary except insofar as it supports human action/feeling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imitation = likeness to appearances, not symbolic representation
rubrics_metrics.description: “A work of art is a likeness (ὁμοίωμα) or reproduction of an original, and not a symbolic representation... mental impressions are not signs or symbols, but copies of external reality, likenesses of the things themselves... art reproduces its original not as it is in itself, but as it appears to the senses.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Artistic imitation aims at a sensible likeness or image rather than arbitrary symbolism. Evaluate art by how convincingly it renders the sensible appearance or phantasm of its objects to the imagination (phantasy), rather than by conventional signs alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Art addresses sensibility and the image-making faculty (phantasy)
rubrics_metrics.description: “Art addresses itself not to the abstract reason but to the sensibility and image-making faculty; it is concerned with outward appearances; it employs illusions; its world is not that which is revealed by pure thought.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Art should engage the audience's sensory/imaginative capacities. Techniques that form and recall vivid images, create after-effects of sensation, or use illusion are central to artistic success. Works should be judged by their capacity to move the sensibility via images and appearances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer internally probable (plausible) impossibilities to externally improbable possibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: “The doctrine of aesthetic semblance and of τὸ πιθανόν... is carried so far that the poet working by illusions ‘ought to prefer probable impossibilities to possible improbabilities.’”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When creating fiction or representation, prioritize internal plausibility and emotional truth over strict factual possibility. A creatively consistent, believable impossibility (within the work's logic) is preferable to an event that is technically possible but feels implausible or inconsistent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human life and inward activity are the primary material of art
rubrics_metrics.description: “The common original, then, from which all the arts draw is human life—its mental processes, its spiritual movements, its outward acts issuing from deeper sources... On this principle landscape and animals are not ranked among the objects of aesthetic imitation.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Art should foreground human psychology, moral character, emotions and motives. External world elements (setting, nature) function chiefly as background or as emotional colouring insofar as they heighten human interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Different arts have distinct powers and must match medium to expressive aim
rubrics_metrics.description: “While all works of art are likenesses... the various arts reflect the image from without by different means and with more or less directness and vividness.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate and produce works with attention to medium-specific capacities: music expresses character and mood via rhythm/melody; painting/sculpture primarily render outward form and rely on conventional signs to suggest inner qualities; poetry can combine words and music. Choose techniques that exploit the strengths of your medium.

rubrics_metrics.name: Music imitates moral character and has ethical/formative power
rubrics_metrics.description: “In rhythms and melodies we have the most realistic imitations of anger and mildness as well as of courage, temperance and all their opposites... Music in reflecting character moulds and influences it.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When composing or assessing music, consider its capacity to represent and shape moral dispositions—especially through rhythm and modal/key choices. Note also that music's ethical import often depends on its association with words, dance, occasion, and cultural conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Art creates aesthetic emotion by imposing form on alien matter (the emancipating power of art)
rubrics_metrics.description: “By the union of a form with a matter, which in the world of experience is alien to it, a magical effect is wrought... The pressure of everyday reality is removed, and the aesthetic emotion is released as an independent activity.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Artistic effectiveness can be achieved by combining form and matter in ways that distance the work from quotidian reality, allowing aesthetic emotions to operate autonomously. This is a device for coherence and for cultivating detached aesthetic responses; use judiciously to achieve the intended emotional effect.
